note.kid: The video is cut into numbered pieces, so nothing gets lost or mixed up.
note.nerd: A reliable, ordered byte stream between two ports: sequence numbers, acknowledgements, retransmits, flow and congestion control.

sealed.kid: Sealed. Only {yours} and the server open this: they check that no pieces are missing.
sealed.nerd: Not inspected on the way: end-to-end between the two ends (ordering, retransmits, congestion control).

line: Transmission Control Protocol, Src Port: {sport}, Dst Port: {dport}, Seq: {seq}, Ack: {ack}

sport.name: Source port
sport.about: Which conversation on the sender. A carrier-grade NAT rewrites it so many customers can share one address.

dport.name: Destination port
dport.about: Which service on the receiver: 443 = HTTPS.

seq.about: Where this data sits in the byte stream, so the receiver can put pieces in order.

ack.name: Acknowledgement
ack.about: The next byte the sender expects from the other side: everything before it arrived.

flags.name: Flags
flags.about: SYN, ACK, PSH, FIN, RST…: what this segment does in the conversation.

window.name: Window
window.about: How much more the sender can take in right now (flow control).

checksum.name: Checksum
checksum.about: Covers the addresses and ports too, so a NAT must fix it when it rewrites them.
